subject: Tracing LLM request path, subprocessors, and erasure commitments
body:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@dovemed.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: trace of request path, subprocessors, and retention windows

Hi Michael,

Thanks for taking the time yesterday on the call. Our security and legal teams need a short, concrete answer set to a few items before we move to internal procurement: where our user payloads (prompt + user metadata) are executed, what third parties touch them, whether any intermediate copies are retained, and how quickly you can erase them on request. Specifically: 

- Can you provide a simple execution map showing which regions and subprocessors a single hosted API call may touch under normal operations (hosted model, not Dedicated)?
- Is there a default retention window for request payloads and model KV caches?
- If we request a full erase for a given customer id, what is the process and guaranteed completion time?
- Do you use any cross-border routing for requests that originate in the US? If yes, what controls do you have to pin execution to a region?

If you have a one-page diagram or an inventory CSV of subprocessors, that would be perfect — our legal wants to attach evidence to the RFP.

Appreciate it,
Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Security, DoveMed
alyssa@dovemed.com

---

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@dovemed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 11:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: trace of request path, subprocessors, and retention windows

Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear list. I put together a concise response below and attached a simple execution diagram plus our current subprocessor inventory CSV. High level first, then the guarantees.

Quick summary (hosted API):
- Execution topology: In our hosted tier a request is accepted in the receiving region (edge), routed to the lowest-latency serving fleet that has capacity (may be in a different region within the same cloud provider family), then the model inference runs on Redwood-managed GPUs.
- Typical subprocessors: Cloud compute (AWS us-west-2, us-east-1; GCP us-central1 for certain model variants), observability (DataDog), object storage for short-term logs (S3 in the processing region), and CDNs for static assets. See attached inventory for full names and contact emails.
- Retention defaults: Customer payloads are retained for 30 days by default for debugging, billing reconciliation, and quality monitoring; we snapshot minimal telemetry (no full prompt backups) beyond that unless retention is extended by you. KV cache (model context cache) is ephemeral and tied to the active session — it is not durable storage and is cleared within minutes to hours depending on activity and cache eviction policies.
- Erasure flow: If you call our Data Deletion API or send a verified erasure request to privacy@redwood.com we start an automated sweep that purges live data and schedules background jobs to delete indexed/batched copies. We commit to substantive deletion of customer payloads within 72 hours and to purge most operational backups within 30 days. For Hosted customers we also provide an evidence pack (log entries showing job completion).
- Cross-border routing: By default, we try to keep execution in-region when capacity and model compatibility allow, but to maintain latency and availability we may route to a nearby compatible region or cloud. If you require strict in-region execution we recommend Dedicated or our Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) which allow region pinning and stronger contractual guarantees.

Attachments included: processing-paths-20261001.svg (diagram), redwood-subprocessor-inventory-20261001.csv (spreadsheet). Also attaching a short erasure playbook.

Notes on the guarantees and edge cases:
1) Shared/default hosted tier: some transient cross-region hops may happen (e.g., edge acceptor in us-west -> compute in us-east) for capacity/fallback. We log the serving region at request time and include it in the evidence pack.
2) Caching: prefix/KV caching is used for performance; it is not a durable store and is evicted per policy. We treat cache eviction separately from payload deletion; an erase request triggers cache invalidation for the relevant keys immediately.
3) Backups: we replicate critical operational state for reliability; our backup retention is separate and we run scheduled deletions — policies vary by account type but for Hosted we commit to removing PII payloads from backups within 30 days of a successful erasure job and to provide audit evidence.
4) Subprocessors: if you need to review subprocessors for export control reasons we can provide a signed inventory and SOC2 attestations or evidence export.

If helpful, Marissa on my team can run through the diagram with your legal folks and produce the signed evidence bundle.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com
(415) 555-0183

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@dovemed.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 08:05:33 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: trace of request path, subprocessors, and retention windows

Thanks Michael — that helps. A couple of follow-ups from legal: 

- The 72-hour erase window: does that cover all copies (live + aggregated logs + backups) or is that just live/operational stores? Legal wants a clear timeline they can show the risk committee.
- On region pinning: is there a configuration flag or policy at the account level to enforce "in-region-only" for hosted? If so what are the limits (models available, throughput impact)?

If you can add a short bullet answer to each and include a sample evidence file structure (what we will receive after you perform the erase), that would close the loop for us.

Best,
Alyssa

---

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@dovemed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 15:03:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: trace of request path, subprocessors, and retention windows

Alyssa — quick bullets to be included in your packet (and I attached a compact evidence example).

- 72-hour window scope: The 72-hour SLA covers removal from active/operational stores (live request logs, customer-facing caches, metadata indexes). Aggregated telemetry and analytics material that may contain non-identifiable derivatives are treated separately; full removal from durable backups is a separate process we complete within 30 days and we provide audit logs showing deletion steps. In short: live purge = 72 hours; durable backup purge = 30 days (evidence included).

- Account-level in-region-only flag (hosted): We offer an "execution_region_pin" account setting for hosted customers. When enabled, we restrict routing and fallbacks to the pinned geographic region or cloud family. Trade-offs: fewer model variants (some large third-party model builds are only in select regions) and possible increased latency or capacity-based throttling during region outages. If you need a strict, contractually-backed guarantee with no cross-region fallbacks, Dedicated or Private deployments are recommended.

- Evidence bundle contents (example):
  - deletion_report.json (timestamped job completion entries)
  - resource_access_log.csv (per-request serving region + node id)
  - subprocessor_contact_list.csv (for legal follow-up)
  - signed_statement_of_deletion.pdf (high level confirmation + signature)

Marissa will follow up to set up a short call with your legal/security team and to produce the signed evidence bundle and SOC2 references. I can also share our sample erasure_playbook PDF if you want.

Let me know what time works for a 30-min review next week — Marissa has availability Tuesday/Wednesday.

Best,
Michael

[Attachment stubs: processing-paths-20261001.svg (diagram), redwood-subprocessor-inventory-20261001.csv (spreadsheet), erasure-playbook-compact.pdf (playbook)]
